text: If what you want is to go back into a painful memory and change how it goes, there's a clinical therapy built for that, called [Imagery Rescripting](https://ibogaqueen.substack.com/i/201523223/imagery-rescripting), which I go into in my somatic guide. It's a lot like the way I [re-do trauma memories](https://ibogaqueen.substack.com/i/189761959/re-do-trauma-memories) in my inner child guide, except that the therapist is there with you in the scene, stepping in as the ideal adult, until you can do that part yourself.
after_block: The main clinical practice guidelines for the treatment of major trauma recommend one or more of the trauma-specific variants of cognitive behavioral therapy (often referred to by specific names, such as cognitive processing therapy, prolonged exposure, etc.) or eye movement desensitization and reprocessing, depending on the person and the guideline. These approaches in turn can be further supported by techniques such as self-hypnosis and inner child work. But high-risk trauma work needs a bigger container than that.

text: If your pain has lasted months and a doctor has found no injury or disease to explain it, I'd also try one of the two talk therapies I go into in [my somatic guide](https://ibogaqueen.substack.com/i/201523223/pain-that-wont-quit), Pain Reprocessing Therapy or Emotional Awareness and Expression Therapy. They've helped people with long-lasting back, muscle and joint pain, by changing their relationship to the pain without pretending it's not there.
after_block: Is there evidence for self-hypnosis? Yes. There has been [a systematic review of Randomized Controlled Trials](https://eprints.bournemouth.ac.uk/31277/4/Eason%20and%20Parris%20in%20press.pdf) of self-hypnosis, finding benefit in studies of pain, childbirth, children, stress, anxiety etc. Self-hypnosis seemed more useful when people learned it as a real skill and practiced it several times than when they just listened to an audio file.

text: If you keep slipping away from feelings in therapy sessions too, like explaining a feeling as soon as it comes up, or agreeing with the therapist just to get past it, I'd look at the three therapies in my somatic guide's section [Can't Stay With a Feeling?](https://ibogaqueen.substack.com/i/201523223/cant-stay-with-a-feeling). One of them, Intensive Short-Term Dynamic Psychotherapy, is built around catching you each time you slip away and asking what you're feeling right then.
after_block: Ask for any diffuse benefits to become more practically focused: "If this is guidance, show me what I need to do about it. If I'm avoiding something, bring me gently back to the present and show me what it is."
